The Geospatial Web Developer provides web application development expertise to support TNC’s diverse and geographically distributed conservation science and marketing communities.

The Geospatial Web Developer will support and develop web GIS applications and solutions according to system requirements following TNC methodologies and best practices. In supporting existing applications and advising professionals across our global organization, they will also play a key role in shaping web application guidelines as we strive for a more consistent approach to web map and application delivery across teams and platforms. While we extensively use Esri tools and technologies, we also use and support other platforms and technologies, including open-source geospatial software.

The Geospatial Web Developer is a member of the Conservation Application Development team but will work with other functional teams in the Conservation & Geospatial Systems group within Information Technology (IT), and with other TNC business units in a variety of development and design roles. The Web Developer will help in creating and maintaining web mapping applications and visualization tools focused on supporting our goal to conserve 4 billion hectares of Earth’s oceans, 650 million hectares of land, 30 million hectares of lakes and wetlands, and 1 million kilometers of river systems. The Geospatial Web Developer will spend approximately 75% of their time designing, developing and maintaining applications and infrastructure, including working with product owners to refine requirements and related tasks, and approximately 25% of their time providing guidance and support to others developing web mapping applications.

This is a fully remote position where the chosen candidate can work anywhere TNC is registered to work with preference to candidates who can serve Eastern and Pacific time zones.

This position is not eligible for relocation, or visa .

Analyze and document end-user and technology-user business requirements for technology projects with wide range of complexity at varying levels of impact on organization-wide initiatives.
Design and develop new, complex technology systems and solutions according to system requirements following TNC methodology and development best practices.
Act as lead technologist on technology application maintenance projects related to application upgrades, conversions, and modifications. Perform tasks assigned as required to complete project including design, development, running specific programs, generating reports, and analyzing results.

jobs.title: Director, Remote Sensing
jobs.description:
WGI is seeking a Director, Remote Sensing
to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. This position is responsible for the people, technology, equipment, processes, and quality systems necessary to successfully execute WGI's airborne remote sensing programs while engaging with leadership of our other Departments.

The Director, Remote Sensing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the Remote Sensing Department. This individual is accountable for departmental performance, staff development, resource planning, technology and equipment strategy, quality, production capacity, and successful project delivery. The Director will maintain sufficient technical expertise to provide oversight, evaluate risk, support complex project decisions, and ensure appropriate technical leadership is available throughout the project lifecycle.

This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team of sensor operators, LiDAR analysts, imagery and photogrammetric professionals, and other geospatial technical staff while coordinating closely with project managers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other WGI disciplines. The Director will be responsible for developing scalable production processes, maintaining high standards for quality and consistency, optimizing staff and equipment utilization, and ensuring that WGI remains at the forefront of remote sensing technology.

This is an in-office leadership position
with travel required to support operations, projects, staff, clients, business development, and field activities.

At WGI, you will find talented, passionate associates providing exceptional service in collaborative, team-driven environments, all while having fun and enjoying the work they do. We work to stay ahead of the curve by investing in the latest tools and technology. As one of the nation’s top consulting firms, we consistently strive to promote efficiency, cultivate a culture our associates can proudly embrace, and empower our associates to advance their career growth at WGI and beyond.

WGI is always looking for remarkable individuals to join our team and help us grow in our vision. If you think you are an innovative, self-motivated team player, and want to shape your community, join our WGI team today!

WGI offers a complete Benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, LTD & STD, Life Insurance, 401k with match, PTO, Holidays, HSA with company contribution, Pet insurance, and Employee Assistance Program.

Operational Leadership: Lead the operations of WGI's Remote Sensing Department, including staffing, production capacity, equipment, resource allocation, workload balancing, project performance, and operational priorities. Establish scalable processes, accountability, and performance measures that support consistent, predictable, and profitable project delivery.
Maintain visibility into backlog, production capacity, staffing availability, equipment utilization, and upcoming project demand to proactively identify resource constraints and develop appropriate staffing, subcontracting, scheduling, or technology solutions.

Airborne Acquisition Operations: Provide operational oversight of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition programs. Ensure qualified technical personnel, appropriate equipment, documented procedures, quality controls, and adequate resources are in place to support safe, efficient, and successful acquisition.
LiDAR & Imagery Production: Provide leadership and technical oversight for WGI's airborne, mobile, terrestrial, and UAS LiDAR and imagery production capabilities. Ensure production teams have effective workflows, appropriate technical leadership, adequate resources, and clearly defined quality standards from initial processing through final delivery.
Quality Management: Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive QA/QC procedures throughout the acquisition and production lifecycle. Establish measurable checkpoints for collection completeness, trajectory quality, relative and absolute accuracy, point density, imagery quality, calibration, classification, data integrity, metadata, and final deliverables. Perform quarterly audits to ensure Project Manager’s compliance to WGI’s established Quality Assurance Program.
Technical Leadership: Maintain strong working knowledge of Remote Sensing technologies, methodologies, specifications, and industry standards. Provide technical oversight for complex projects, support technical decision-making, and ensure appropriate subject-matter experts are engaged to resolve specialized technical issues. Develop and empower technical leaders within the department rather than creating dependency on a single technical resource.
Project Delivery: Maintain visibility across active Remote Sensing projects and proactively address schedule, staffing, technical, equipment, or quality issues that could affect successful delivery. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.
People Leadership: Lead, mentor, develop, and evaluate Remote Sensing staff and technical leaders. Establish clear expectations, accountability, career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities. Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.
Equipment & Technology Management: Oversee the effective deployment, maintenance, calibration, and lifecycle planning of remote sensing sensors, GNSS/IMU systems, computing infrastructure, storage, and supporting equipment. Participate in evaluation and justification of significant technology and capital investments.
Automation & Process Improvement: Promote automation, batch processing, scripting, and standardized production workflows to improve quality, repeatability, throughput, and cost efficiency. Identify production bottlenecks and implement measurable improvements.
Technical Risk & Issue Resolution: Ensure complex technical, equipment, software, processing, and data-quality issues are appropriately escalated, investigated, and resolved. Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.
Financial & Resource Management: Assist with the development of department budgets, staffing plans, capital expenditures, equipment utilization, project performance, and resource forecasting. Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.
Business Development & Client Support: Support WGI's business development activities through technical presentations, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, project approaches, and client meetings. Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.
Innovation: Evaluate emerging LiDAR, imagery, UAS, positioning, cloud-computing, AI/ML, and geospatial technologies. Recommend technologies and investments that improve WGI's capabilities, productivity, quality, or competitive position.
Safety & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture across airborne, vehicle-based, UAS, and field operations. Ensure departmental activities comply with WGI policies, applicable regulations, aviation requirements, client requirements, professional standards, and established operating procedures.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Surveying, GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline preferred; advanced degree a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.
Data: Management of large point-cloud and imagery datasets, high-performance processing environments, network/cloud storage, metadata, archival and data-transfer workflows.

Preferred Licenses & Certifications

Professional credentials should be considered favorably and may be factored into position level and compensation, including:

ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist (CP)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Scientist - LiDAR (CMS-LiDAR)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Technician - LiDAR (CMT-LiDAR)
Professional Surveyor/Professional Land Surveyor licensure
Surveyor Intern/LSIT certification
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
Other relevant geospatial, photogrammetric, aviation, project-management, or technical certifications

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the U.S. on a full-time basis. We are unable to sponsor or take over the sponsorship of employment visas.

Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.

Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Geothermal Senior Planner (Environmental Planner 4)
within the Shorelands & Environmental Assistance
(SEA) program.

Note
: This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. It may be extended based on funding availability.

Location:

This position can be based at any of the following duty stations:

Headquarters Office in Lacey, WA .
Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Eastern Region Office in Spokane, WA .
Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, WA .

Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the selected duty station.

Note: If the selected duty station is the Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, the salary will include an additional 5% premium pay due to its location in King County. Salary range: $6703- $9012 monthly.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
One to two days per week of on-site attendance is required
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Duties

This Geothermal Senior Planner position provides a unique opportunity to lead Washington’s emerging statewide geothermal energy planning and policy efforts within Ecology’s Shorelands & Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program. In this role, you will guide multi-agency collaboration, facilitate complex policy discussions, and deliver high-visibility legislative and technical reports that inform Washington’s transition to clean energy. You will serve as a senior planning consultant to the Clean Energy Coordination Section Manager, shaping policy direction, supporting future statewide planning and rulemaking, and ensuring consistent, transparent, and legally defensible processes related to geothermal development.

You will also support Ecology’s coordination of the geothermal energy collaborative process established by the Legislature—bringing together state agencies, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community interests to identify risks, opportunities, and regulatory needs associated with geothermal technologies. Through this work, you will develop guidance, regulatory gap analyses, outreach materials, environmental review support, and planning documents that advance agency priorities and contribute to the long-term protection and sustainable use of Washington’s natural resources.

What You Will Do

Support Ecology’s statewide geothermal energy collaborative process, managing cross-program and multi-agency teams to develop legislative reports, technical analyses, environmental review support, and statewide guidance documents.
Coordinate with experts across Ecology, other state agencies, federal partners, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community groups to ensure inclusive, informed, and well-aligned planning and environmental review processes.
Research existing regulatory frameworks and conduct regulatory gap analyses to evaluate the need for future statewide planning, policy development, and rulemaking related to geothermal energy.
Provide senior-level planning, policy interpretation, and technical consultation to Ecology leadership, program managers, and staff on geothermal topics, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) processes, regulatory implications, and interagency coordination.
Facilitate resolution of complex, sensitive, and high-profile issues involving diverse perspectives, technical uncertainty, emerging technologies, and major environmental considerations.
Support SEPA planning and project review activities by coordinating technical input, reviewing impact analyses, and ensuring documents are clear, consistent, and meet procedural and legal standards.
Plan, coordinate, and conduct public meetings, hearings, workshops, and comment periods, developing accessible materials and ensuring meaningful engagement of Tribes, community members, and interested parties.

The Refrigerant Management Program (RMP) regulates facilities with large refrigeration and air-conditioning systems to ensure they follow best practices that reduce leaks of climate-polluting fluorinated gases. The Geospatial Web Developer provides web application development expertise to support TNC’s diverse and geographically distributed conservation science and marketing communities.

The Geospatial Web Developer is a member of the Conservation Application Development team but will work with other functional teams in the Conservation & Geospatial Systems group within Information Technology (IT), and with other TNC business units in a variety of development and design roles. The Web Developer will help in creating and maintaining web mapping applications and visualization tools focused on supporting our goal to conserve 4 billion hectares of Earth’s oceans, 650 million hectares of land, 30 million hectares of lakes and wetlands, and 1 million kilometers of river systems. The Geospatial Web Developer will spend approximately 75% of their time designing, developing and maintaining applications and infrastructure, including working with product owners to refine requirements and related tasks, and approximately 25% of their time providing guidance and support to others developing web mapping applications.

This is a fully remote position where the chosen candidate can work anywhere TNC is registered to work with preference to candidates who can serve Eastern and Pacific time zones.

This position is not eligible for relocation, or visa .

Responsibilities & Scope

Analyze and document end-user and technology-user business requirements for technology projects with wide range of complexity at varying levels of impact on organization-wide initiatives.
Design and develop new, complex technology systems and solutions according to system requirements following TNC methodology and development best practices.

Learn continuously and seek opportunities to grow as a developer.

Bachelor's degree in computer science, or a related field and three years of experience in programming and systems design OR an equivalent combination of education and/or experience.

Experience with UI/UX, web design and usability principles in application development.

Experience analyzing complex, system-wide technical specifications, debugging applications, and producing effective user and technical documentation.

Desired Qualifications

Ability to work on projects independently and with a team of developers.
Experience using AI coding assistants for accelerating development tasks.
Experience in both cartographic and graphic design, including mapping and charting libraries (e.g., Chart.js, amCharts, D3).
Experience with ArcGIS Online (AGO) tools and platforms (e.g., Experience Builder, AGO dashboards).
Backend development experience (experience with .NET/C# is a plus).
Knowledge of database management systems (e.g., Esri’s File Geodatabase, PostgresSQL/PostGIS, AWS RDS, AWS Aurora, Microsoft SQL Server, or MySQL).
Knowledge of and experience with cloud computing services (AWS preferred).
Experience with Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) and deployment pipelines.
Experience with app containerization (e.g., Docker).
Leadership skills and an ability to coordinate application delivery and best practices across different organizational units.
Strong interest or a background in natural sciences and conservation.
Strong time management skills and the ability to prioritize multiple competing demands.
Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience are appreciated, including experience with web maps supporting different languages.

to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.

Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.

Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.

Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.

Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.

10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.

new_jobs.description:
WGI is seeking a Director, Remote Sensing
to lead the operations and technical delivery of our Remote Sensing Department within the Geospatial Division. This position is responsible for the people, technology, equipment, processes, and quality systems necessary to successfully execute WGI's airborne remote sensing programs while engaging with leadership of our other Departments.

The Director, Remote Sensing will provide strategic, operational, and technical leadership for the Remote Sensing Department. This individual is accountable for departmental performance, staff development, resource planning, technology and equipment strategy, quality, production capacity, and successful project delivery. The Director will maintain sufficient technical expertise to provide oversight, evaluate risk, support complex project decisions, and ensure appropriate technical leadership is available throughout the project lifecycle.

This individual will lead a multidisciplinary team of sensor operators, LiDAR analysts, imagery and photogrammetric professionals, and other geospatial technical staff while coordinating closely with project managers, surveyors, GIS professionals, and other WGI disciplines. The Director will be responsible for developing scalable production processes, maintaining high standards for quality and consistency, optimizing staff and equipment utilization, and ensuring that WGI remains at the forefront of remote sensing technology.

This is an in-office leadership position
with travel required to support operations, projects, staff, clients, business development, and field activities.

At WGI, you will find talented, passionate associates providing exceptional service in collaborative, team-driven environments, all while having fun and enjoying the work they do. We work to stay ahead of the curve by investing in the latest tools and technology. As one of the nation’s top consulting firms, we consistently strive to promote efficiency, cultivate a culture our associates can proudly embrace, and empower our associates to advance their career growth at WGI and beyond.

WGI is always looking for remarkable individuals to join our team and help us grow in our vision. If you think you are an innovative, self-motivated team player, and want to shape your community, join our WGI team today!

WGI offers a complete Benefits package including: Medical, Dental, Vision, LTD & STD, Life Insurance, 401k with match, PTO, Holidays, HSA with company contribution, Pet insurance, and Employee Assistance Program.

Compensation Range:
$175,000 - $200,000

Operational Leadership: Lead the operations of WGI's Remote Sensing Department, including staffing, production capacity, equipment, resource allocation, workload balancing, project performance, and operational priorities. Establish scalable processes, accountability, and performance measures that support consistent, predictable, and profitable project delivery.
Maintain visibility into backlog, production capacity, staffing availability, equipment utilization, and upcoming project demand to proactively identify resource constraints and develop appropriate staffing, subcontracting, scheduling, or technology solutions.

Airborne Acquisition Operations: Provide operational oversight of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition programs. Ensure qualified technical personnel, appropriate equipment, documented procedures, quality controls, and adequate resources are in place to support safe, efficient, and successful acquisition.
LiDAR & Imagery Production: Provide leadership and technical oversight for WGI's airborne, mobile, terrestrial, and UAS LiDAR and imagery production capabilities. Ensure production teams have effective workflows, appropriate technical leadership, adequate resources, and clearly defined quality standards from initial processing through final delivery.
Quality Management: Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive QA/QC procedures throughout the acquisition and production lifecycle. Establish measurable checkpoints for collection completeness, trajectory quality, relative and absolute accuracy, point density, imagery quality, calibration, classification, data integrity, metadata, and final deliverables. Perform quarterly audits to ensure Project Manager’s compliance to WGI’s established Quality Assurance Program.
Technical Leadership: Maintain strong working knowledge of Remote Sensing technologies, methodologies, specifications, and industry standards. Provide technical oversight for complex projects, support technical decision-making, and ensure appropriate subject-matter experts are engaged to resolve specialized technical issues. Develop and empower technical leaders within the department rather than creating dependency on a single technical resource.
Project Delivery: Maintain visibility across active Remote Sensing projects and proactively address schedule, staffing, technical, equipment, or quality issues that could affect successful delivery. Coordinate with project managers to establish realistic schedules, production plans, budgets, and resource requirements.
People Leadership: Lead, mentor, develop, and evaluate Remote Sensing staff and technical leaders. Establish clear expectations, accountability, career paths, succession plans, and development opportunities. Identify staffing and training needs, build technical depth and redundancy, and develop future leaders capable of independently managing critical technical and operational functions.
Equipment & Technology Management: Oversee the effective deployment, maintenance, calibration, and lifecycle planning of remote sensing sensors, GNSS/IMU systems, computing infrastructure, storage, and supporting equipment. Participate in evaluation and justification of significant technology and capital investments.
Automation & Process Improvement: Promote automation, batch processing, scripting, and standardized production workflows to improve quality, repeatability, throughput, and cost efficiency. Identify production bottlenecks and implement measurable improvements.
Technical Risk & Issue Resolution: Ensure complex technical, equipment, software, processing, and data-quality issues are appropriately escalated, investigated, and resolved. Facilitate root-cause analysis and ensure lessons learned are incorporated into standards, training, and operating procedures.
Standards & Procedures: Establish and maintain departmental standards, standard operating procedures, production workflows, technical documentation, and QA/QC requirements to promote consistent execution across staff, offices, technologies, and projects.
Financial & Resource Management: Assist with the development of department budgets, staffing plans, capital expenditures, equipment utilization, project performance, and resource forecasting. Monitor and manage to key operational and financial performance indicators and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.
Business Development & Client Support: Support WGI's business development activities through technical presentations, proposal development, scopes of work, level-of-effort estimates, project approaches, and client meetings. Assist project managers and business development professionals in developing technically sound and competitive remote sensing solutions.
Innovation: Evaluate emerging LiDAR, imagery, UAS, positioning, cloud-computing, AI/ML, and geospatial technologies. Recommend technologies and investments that improve WGI's capabilities, productivity, quality, or competitive position.
Safety & Compliance: Promote a strong safety culture across airborne, vehicle-based, UAS, and field operations. Ensure departmental activities comply with WGI policies, applicable regulations, aviation requirements, client requirements, professional standards, and established operating procedures.
Bachelor's degree in Geomatics, Surveying, GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Photogrammetry, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline preferred; advanced degree a plus.
10+ years of progressive experience in LiDAR, photogrammetry, remote sensing, surveying, mapping, or related geospatial disciplines, with significant experience leading technical teams and complex projects.
Demonstrated experience managing remote sensing production operations involving multiple concurrent projects, staff, equipment, and significant volumes of geospatial data.
Strong working knowledge of airborne LiDAR and imagery acquisition and production sufficient to provide technical oversight, evaluate project risk, and guide technical decision-making. Broad understanding of GNSS/IMU trajectory processing, sensor calibration, boresight adjustment, strip/swath alignment, relative and absolute accuracy, point cloud processing, imagery workflows, and geospatial QA/QC.
Experience with mobile and terrestrial LiDAR and UAS LiDAR/imagery strongly preferred.
Advanced knowledge of remote sensing data management, coordinate systems, projections, horizontal and vertical datums, transformations, survey control, and accuracy assessment.
Experience developing and implementing documented production and QA/QC procedures.
Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical, operational, and production issues.
Experience managing technical staff, developing employees, allocating resources, and improving operational performance.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects, schedules, priorities, and deadlines.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to collaborate across WGI's Geospatial, Transportation, Civil, and Buildings disciplines and work effectively with project managers, technical leaders, clients, subcontractors, and partners.

Technical Experience

The ideal candidate will bring broad remote sensing experience and significant expertise in several of the following areas:

Sensors/Platforms: RIEGL, Leica and Trimble LiDAR systems; airborne LiDAR and digital imagery systems; mobile mapping systems; terrestrial/static scanning; and UAS LiDAR and imagery platforms.
Primary Software: RiPROCESS, Applanix POSPac and TopoDOT.
Additional Software: TerraSolid, Inertial Explorer, MicroStation, ArcGIS Pro, LP360, Leica/Cyclone environments, GeoCue and other industry-standard LiDAR, photogrammetric, CAD and GIS applications.
Processing: GNSS/IMU trajectory development; point cloud generation; calibration; boresight and strip adjustment; registration; classification; tiling; imagery processing; orthorectification; feature extraction; surface generation; accuracy assessment; and final deliverable development.
Automation: Batch processing, scripting, macros, automated QA/QC and other approaches that increase production efficiency and repeatability.
Data: Management of large point-cloud and imagery datasets, high-performance processing environments, network/cloud storage, metadata, archival and data-transfer workflows.

Preferred Licenses & Certifications

Professional credentials should be considered favorably and may be factored into position level and compensation, including:

ASPRS Certified Photogrammetrist (CP)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Scientist - LiDAR (CMS-LiDAR)
ASPRS Certified Mapping Technician - LiDAR (CMT-LiDAR)
Professional Surveyor/Professional Land Surveyor licensure
Surveyor Intern/LSIT certification
FAA Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate
Other relevant geospatial, photogrammetric, aviation, project-management, or technical certifications

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Geothermal Senior Planner (Environmental Planner 4)

(SEA) program.

: This is a temporary position that will end on June 30, 2027. It may be extended based on funding availability.

Northwest Region Office in Shoreline, WA .

Schedule

One to two days per week of on-site attendance is required
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Duties

This Geothermal Senior Planner position provides a unique opportunity to lead Washington’s emerging statewide geothermal energy planning and policy efforts within Ecology’s Shorelands & Environmental Assistance (SEA) Program. In this role, you will guide multi-agency collaboration, facilitate complex policy discussions, and deliver high-visibility legislative and technical reports that inform Washington’s transition to clean energy. You will serve as a senior planning consultant to the Clean Energy Coordination Section Manager, shaping policy direction, supporting future statewide planning and rulemaking, and ensuring consistent, transparent, and legally defensible processes related to geothermal development.

You will also support Ecology’s coordination of the geothermal energy collaborative process established by the Legislature—bringing together state agencies, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community interests to identify risks, opportunities, and regulatory needs associated with geothermal technologies. Through this work, you will develop guidance, regulatory gap analyses, outreach materials, environmental review support, and planning documents that advance agency priorities and contribute to the long-term protection and sustainable use of Washington’s natural resources.

What You Will Do

Support Ecology’s statewide geothermal energy collaborative process, managing cross-program and multi-agency teams to develop legislative reports, technical analyses, environmental review support, and statewide guidance documents.
Coordinate with experts across Ecology, other state agencies, federal partners, Tribal governments, local governments, industry, utilities, and community groups to ensure inclusive, informed, and well-aligned planning and environmental review processes.
Research existing regulatory frameworks and conduct regulatory gap analyses to evaluate the need for future statewide planning, policy development, and rulemaking related to geothermal energy.
Provide senior-level planning, policy interpretation, and technical consultation to Ecology leadership, program managers, and staff on geothermal topics, State Environmental Policy Act (SEPA) processes, regulatory implications, and interagency coordination.
Facilitate resolution of complex, sensitive, and high-profile issues involving diverse perspectives, technical uncertainty, emerging technologies, and major environmental considerations.
Support SEPA planning and project review activities by coordinating technical input, reviewing impact analyses, and ensuring documents are clear, consistent, and meet procedural and legal standards.
Plan, coordinate, and conduct public meetings, hearings, workshops, and comment periods, developing accessible materials and ensuring meaningful engagement of Tribes, community members, and interested parties.
Represent Ecology at multi-agency workgroups, public forums, advisory committees, and policy discussions related to geothermal development, clean energy planning, and statewide environmental review.
Develop and refine tools, guidance, and communication products—working closely with internal and external communications experts—to ensure information is accurate, transparent, and accessible to diverse audiences.
Ensure all deliverables, including legislative reports and technical documents, are efficient, effective, defensible, and aligned with agency policy, scientific information, and interested parties expectations.
Support broader Clean Energy Coordination Section priorities by contributing to statewide planning documents, environmental reviews, interagency coordination efforts, and rulemaking activities related to clean energy development.

Nine years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which includes the following:

Environmental Review: Ability to support complex SEPA environmental review processes, coordinate technical input across programs, interpret impact analyses, and ensure documents meet legal and procedural requirements.
Regulatory Analysis: Ability to analyze and implement federal, state, and local regulations and synthesize technical and regulatory information.
Policy and Planning Analysis: Ability to analyze environmental data, evaluate planning and regulatory implications, and develop recommendations grounded in scientific information and agency policy.

Schedule

Application Timeline

Apply by October 4, 2026.
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

Do you want your work to directly reduce climate-polluting emissions in Washington State? Does the idea of helping businesses understand and comply with environmental regulations appeal to you? Are you interested in conducting on-the-ground inspections and working one-on-one with the regulated community to keep refrigerant systems operating safely and responsibly? If you answered “yes,” then this role may be a great fit for you!

The Refrigerant Management Program (RMP) regulates facilities with large refrigeration and air-conditioning systems to ensure they follow best practices that reduce leaks of climate-polluting fluorinated gases. As a Regional Compliance Inspector, you will help facilities register in the RMP, provide technical guidance, and conduct inspections across the Northwest region to verify compliance.

Your work will directly support Ecology’s statewide effort to reduce greenhouse gas emissions from refrigeration systems. You will develop specialized knowledge of Washington’s hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) regulations, interpret technical requirements for the public, and help facilities identify practical, cost-effective ways to meet their obligations. If you are motivated by fieldwork, enjoy problem-solving, and want your work to contribute to meaningful climate solutions, this position offers a rewarding opportunity.

In This Role, You Will

Provide technical assistance to facility owners and operators, helping them understand refrigerant rules, reporting obligations, and how to comply with RMP processes.
Explain refrigerant regulations in a clear, accessible way during one-on-one interactions, online office hours, and public meetings.
Assist facility owners and operators with entering required data into the Refrigeration and Air-Conditioning Management Program (RAMP) database.

Conduct inspections of facilities subject to the Refrigerant Management Program (RMP), both remotely and in person.
Verify that facilities are following state and federal HFC rules and maintaining records that meet program requirements.
Review RMP registrations and annual reports, identify potential compliance issues, and help return facilities to compliance through follow-up actions.
If necessary, collect and document information necessary for enforcement actions.

Coordinate with teammates across the state to ensure consistent application of inspection procedures and regulatory interpretations, and on potential ways to improve compliance.
Collaborate with Ecology outreach staff to promote awareness of climate-friendly refrigerants and refrigerant alternatives.
Develop/maintain professional knowledge of applicable HFC laws, refrigerant technologies, leak detection methods, and emerging industry issues.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education related to the duties of the position, which must include the following:

Regulatory Application and Interpretation – Demonstrated competence with interpreting and applying environmental or regulatory requirements to accurately assess facility compliance and support consistent implementation of program obligations.
Inspection and Field Evaluation – Experienced in conducting structured compliance inspections or field evaluations to determine whether facilities follow required procedures and maintain accurate operational or recordkeeping practices.
Professional Judgment and Compliance Determination – Skilled at using analytical thinking, evidence review, and sound professional judgment to identify potential violations, recommend corrective actions, and support facilities in returning to sustained compliance.
Technical Assistance and Communication – Ability to explain complex regulatory or technical information in clear, understandable terms to help regulated entities meet program requirements and successfully use required database tools.
Collaborative Coordination Across Teams – Demonstrated competence with coordinating work and sharing information across the regional inspection team to ensure consistent approaches to inspections, education, compliance assistance, and enforcement activities.
Data, System, and Technology Proficiency – Skilled with learning and using program-specific databases and analytical tools to track inspection activities, organize documentation, analyze compliance trends, and prepare accurate reports that support program decision-making.
Independent Project and Workload Management – Ability to independently plan, prioritize, and complete inspections, follow-up activities, and documentation to meet program expectations and support timely, effective compliance outcomes.
Research and Emerging Issues Analysis – Experienced in gaining understanding of new or evolving technical, regulatory, or environmental issues to identify trends, evaluate potential impacts on program implementation, and recommend improvements that strengthen compliance and reduce emissions.

Education
involving a major study in environmental, physical, or one of the natural sciences; Environmental Health or Occupational Safety and Health (OSHA) studies; environmental planning, or an academic discipline related to the duties of the position.

Desired Qualifications

Environmental Compliance and Inspection Experience – Experienced in performing environmental compliance, inspection, or auditing work to assess facility operations, evaluate records or procedures, and recommend corrective actions that strengthen adherence to regulatory requirements.
Climate and Air Quality Knowledge – Demonstrated competence with understanding air quality concepts and climate change science to evaluate how refrigerant emissions and compliance activities support statewide emission reduction goals.
Greenhouse Gas Program Familiarity – Experienced in working with state or federal greenhouse gas reduction programs to understand how HFC-related requirements fit within broader regulatory or climate-policy frameworks.
Program-Specific Technical Learning – Ability to quickly learn and apply new technical subject matter, including refrigerant types, climate-friendly alternatives, and leak detection methods, to support high-quality inspections and compliance assistance.
